text:
sasha: Heads-up — saw an OOM on prod-rt-3 while running a ~10k-token session. KV cache pages shot up and eviction churn was through the roof. stack trace/snippet in a bit.
maya: ugh. any user-visible errors? latency spike?
sasha: clients saw intermittent 503s and stalled streams for ~30s, then fallback to smaller model worked. latency for other requests on that host also spiked.
evan: can you paste the small telemetry? evan: please include pmap and slab stats.
sasha: sure — quick dump:
```
host=prod-rt-3 evict_rate=127/s kv_pages_alloc=1.9GiB kv_pages_in_use=1.84GiB page_faults=4823
slab_free=48MiB slab_frag=18% cache_reuse_hit=0.62
```
li: that eviction rate looks like thrashing. is this long-prefix growth or leak in reuse window?
sasha: looks tied to one very long conversation that kept extending tokens; prefix growth + repeated selective replays of earlier segments. reuse hit ratio decreased as the context grew.
ryan: rough repro plan: replay the session from the chronicle with incremental sampling at 2x speed, watch reuse hit decay. I can start a replay job.
maya: also check kernel selection — did we switch to the quant kernel unexpectedly? That can increase transient memory if we allocate fallbacks.
evan: good point. i see in the runtime logs an immediate kernel switch at t+2m for that session: fallback->float16_nonopt because of alignment mismatch. that path does extra staging buffers.
ops-bot: deploybot: alert created #INC-7684 for prod-rt-3 OOM, assigned to eng-runtime.
sasha: notes from crashdump: OOM happened during kv_page_serialize(), backtrace shows heavy memcpy in slow-path.
li: memcpy heavy suggests paging movement; if the slab allocator can't coalesce free spans we end up with fragmented free space and lots of small evictions.
ryan: suspect interplay: kernel switch -> staging buffers -> less free slab -> small fragments -> eviction thrash -> OOM.
maya: mitigation checklist proposal:
- soft-degrade: when host sees evict_rate > 100/s AND reuse_hit < 0.7 for 30s, throttle new long-session starts and redirect to dedicated-capacity pool
- aggressive prefix trimming: trim stale prefixes older than 6k tokens for sessions that haven't been active in 120s
- eviction backoff: add exponential backoff on retrying the same page for 3 rounds before forcing compact
- kernel pin: disallow dynamic kernel fallback to float16_nonopt when free slab < 200MiB
- telemetry: emit kv_frag_ratio, avg_free_span, last_kernel_change

sasha: I like kernel pin and backoff. prefix trimming is risky for user experience but ok as a controlled soft-degrade.
evan: can add a temporary routing rule in traffic-gate to move new long-lived sessions to a non-shared pool. i'll do that now for prod-rt-3's AZ as a canary.
li: for compaction, we should try a quick coalesce pass that avoids stopping token generation: incremental coalesce per-slab-thread with slice budget 10ms.
ryan: i can prototype the incremental coalesce in a feature branch and run microbenchmarks. want to measure wall-time pause and fragmentation reduction.
sasha: experiment idea: synthetic workload that ramps token appends on a single session to 20k tokens, and another workload that repeatedly reads prefixes to reduce reuse. compare with/without kernel pin and with/without incremental coalesce.
maya: also check whether batching heuristics are amplifying the problem — continuous batching may aggregate many sessions onto the same worker; maybe reduce continuous batch max size for hosts with low free slab.
evan: good call. we can add batch_size_soft_limit that responds to free memory signals.
ops-bot: note: incident updated — mitigation in progress, routing rule applied to AZ-A.
li: quick queries I ran:
- top evicting session ids: sess-773, sess-774 (the long one is sess-773)
- avg reuse hit pre-incident: 0.78, during incident: 0.59
- kernel changes: 1 kernel switch observed at 1759992330

ryan: action items:
- r1 (ryan): implement incremental coalesce POC (branch kv-coalesce-poc)
- r2 (evan): add kernel pin config guard in runtime and a feature flag
- r3 (maya): add traffic-gate rule to route new long sessions away from shared pool (canary applied)
- r4 (li): add telemetry kv_frag_ratio and avg_free_span to metrics
- r5 (sasha): produce reproducible trace and upload core dump

sasha: i've uploaded the trace to S3: s3://redwood-prod-dumps/prod-rt-3/1759992468/trace.tar.gz
maya: i've lowered continuous batch max from 64 -> 32 on the canary hosts and will monitor.
li: next steps — let's convene a short sync in 15m to decide on rollout of kernel-pin and prefix trimming thresholds.
ryan: noted. i'll have numbers for coalesce POC by EOD.
ops-bot: incident closed? temporarily mitigated — follow-ups tracked in INC-7684.
maya: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
